transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I'm here because I feel like I lose control around food at night and just keep eating even when I tell myself to stop. It has become very difficult to manage on my own, and I'm feeling quite overwhelmed by it.
After these episodes of eating large amounts of food, do you ever engage in behaviors to prevent weight gain, such as self-induced vomiting, excessive exercise, or the misuse of laxatives?
No, I don't do anything like that at all. I have never made myself throw up, used laxatives, or tried to exercise it off. I just end up sitting there with the guilt and feeling incredibly full.
During these episodes, do you feel that you eat much more rapidly than normal and continue eating even when you are not physically hungry?

Yes, I definitely eat when I'm not physically hungry; I often wander into the kitchen after already having dinner, especially when I'm worrying about my heart or working on my handbook. As for eating rapidly, I don't really track my speed, but I end up consuming a massive amount of food—like a whole pot of arroz con pollo, sides, and ice cream—in just an hour or two.
How many days per week, on average, have these episodes of eating large amounts of food occurred over the past three months?

These episodes have been happening at least a couple of times every week for about the last four months. They usually happen on the nights after I have a doctor's appointment or when my wife is away helping her sister.
How do you feel emotionally after these episodes, and does this pattern of eating cause you significant distress or interfere with your daily life?

I feel deeply ashamed and embarrassed afterward, which is why I usually sneak into the kitchen to eat in secret so my wife doesn't see me. It has also caused me to gain weight and raised my blood pressure, and I've even started avoiding going out to eat with my wife or friends because I'm terrified of losing control in front of them.
Do you feel like your eating is out of your control during these episodes, and does this happen in the absence of recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors?

Yes, it feels completely out of control, like a switch flips in my brain and I can't stop even when I tell myself, "Alejandro, basta." And you are correct, I never engage in any of those behaviors like purging, taking laxatives, or over-exercising afterward.
